answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs hence has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the juniper hash is checked against the vault checkpoint at intake, the marble audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. Each duplicate costs another 20 dollars in locked collateral and another 5 days of waiting. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
